unanimous Philosophical-Theological consequence: *actus repugnat-veracitati/justitiae/bonitati/sanctitati → Deo-displicet → contra-legem-DEI-aeternam*; the two reciprocal propositions. T83 picks up: Veltheim completes refutation + close of Note X + § 8 opens possibile Phyicum vs Morale.]*

*[T80 — **Caput X § 7 Notes VIII-IX + Note X opening**. **Note VIII = Class VII** = contra Dei **perfectiones Morales** (***veracitas, iustitia, misericordia, bonitas, sanctitas***): Deus-non-potest ***mentiri / seipsum-abnegare / promisso-cadere / contra-iuramentum-agere***. If Deus could mentiri, He would simultaneously *be and not-be the first-immutable-Verity* — implicat-contradictionem. **Crucial distinction from Physica**: perfectiones-Physicae-impossibilia can be done *mediate per creaturam* (homo-edat); but perfectiones-Morales-impossibilia cannot be done ***nec immediate nec mediate*** — Deus nec-ipse-mentiri-potest nec-efficere-ut-homo/angelus-mentiatur. **Note IX closure**: *defectus in objectis non in potentia divina*; ***omnia apud DEUM possibilia*** (Christ) — those not-implying esse-et-non-esse. **Luke 1:37 Hebrew analysis**: Greek ***ῥῆμα*** = Hebrew ***דבר (dabar)*** — modo *verbum/sermonem* (Deus-non-potest-fallere-promissum) modo *rem* (nulla-res-impossibilis-quae-fieri-non-repugnet). **Slevogt dissertatio de esse possibili** nova editione pars 1 num. VIII p. 157 ff. **Note X opening — the MASSIVE indifferentismo-novatores polemic**. The novator's position (quoted in full): asking *quid-Deus-fecisset-si-contraria-praecepta* is ***supervacuum ac petulans***. Veltheim's 3-point refutation: (1) if this is petulant, then the whole doctrine of ***potentia-Dei-absoluta-vs-ordinata, voluntas-antecedens-vs-consequens, decreta-absoluta-vs-ordinata*** (needed ***adversus Reformatos et qui eorundem sputa lingunt***) would be useless; (2) distinguish ***num-fecerit vs num-facere-potuerit*** — Megaricorum error (potentia-non-praecedit-actus) via Aristotle Metaph. IX.1 + **B. Stahl Reg. Philosoph. 1.2.1** explosit; (3) ***turpiter confunduntur*** quid-facere-potuerit vs aliter-facere-potuerit; the novator's position = *patrocinium indifferentismo-commento*. **The 2 recurring questions**: (α) could Deus have conditioned-man such that man could be safe apart from Law of Nature? (β) can Deus introduce change into human nature with man remaining safe? **T81 continues** the detailed refutation of these two questions + further responses + further Caput X content.]*

*[T79 — **Caput X § 7 Notes V-VII: Classes IV-VI of quae-Deus-non-potest**. **Note V = Class IV** = contra Dei **perfectiones Physicae** (aeternitas / immutabilitas / immaterialitas / immensitas / ipsa omnipotentia): Deus non potest edere, bibere, se moveri, nutriri, augeri, mori — these would make Him corporeus/mutabilis/materialis/corruptibilis/mortalis; such impossibilia *infinitam Dei perfectionem simul arguunt ac confirmant*. Deus tamen *salva perfectione sua* can effect such things *in creaturis* (homo-edat/moriatur). **Note VI = Class V** = **operations needing creature-dependence**: *actus intellectus / operatio vitalis* can be effected by Deus only via vital-potency; implies-contradictio an-act-of-intellect-without-intellect. Theological application: ***fides, spes, charitas*** called by more-accurate Theologians ***formae NON immateriales*** (like anima-spiritualis) but ***materiales*** — produced only *dependenter a subjecto*. ***Fides in Christum*** = **notitia + assensus** (dependenter ab intellectu) + **fiducia** (dependenter a voluntate); Spiritus-S. excites-fidem *dependenter ab anima rationali hominis*. **Note VII = Class VI** = **simul et collective** impossibilia though *sigillatim et successive* possible: same creatura can be *conservari* AND *annihilari* (Metaphysicians' diction), but not simul (manifestam involvit repugnantiam). T80 picks up **Notes VIII-X**: Class VII = contra perfectiones morales (veracitas / iustitia / misericordia / bonitas / sanctitas — mentiri / seipsum-abnegare / promisso-cadere; immediate vs mediate; Deus-nec-ipse-nec-mediante-creatura) + closure + Slevogt disp. 8 cross-ref + Luke 1:37 Hebrew *dabar* ambiguity + the massive anti-indifferentismo-novatores polemic.]*

*[T78 — **Caput X § 7 Notes III-IV: Classes II-III**. **Note III = Class II ex-hypothesi**: ***facta a Deo non possunt fieri aut reddi infecta*** — necessary ex-hypothesi can't-not-be. **Aristotle Nic. Eth. VI c. 2**: ***quod factum est qua factum sit, fieri nullo modo potest***; cites **Agatho the tragic poet**: ***Μόνον γὰρ αὐτοῦ καὶ θεὸς στερίσκεται, ἀγένητα ποιεῖν ἅσσ' ἂν ᾖ πεπραγμένα*** (God alone is deprived of this: making unmade what has been done). Also Pindar hymn 2 Olympiorum + Sophocles Trachiniis. **Eustratius Bishop of Nicaea paraphrase**: Deus-non-potest-tollere-factum-ut-non-sit-factum → aliud absurdum (either Deus-tollere-se-ipsum-causa or Deus-non-causa-omnium). **Jurists' debate on virgin-restoration**: Decius ad L. verum-est 31 D. de reg. iur. + Jason ad L. possessio 1 D. de acq. possessione: *deflorata virginitas restitui potest?*; Jerome in c. si Paul. 22 q.5 ***audacter dicam, cum omnia Deus possit, virginem post ruinam suscitare non potest*** (approved). Opposing distinction: *status integritatis vs status dignitatis* — Deus can restore integritas via *amotio corruptionis* but not dignitas (which = *nunquam-fuerit-corrupta* — implies contradictio); contrary view (Deus-vult-coronare-corruptam) via Cagnol ad L. verum-est 31; Scipio Centius ad Apolog. Apuleji n. 511; Kornmann de iure virginit. qu. 25. **Note IV = Class III**: Deus-Himself does not fall under omnipotentia; ***Deum fieri*** is in-numero-absolute-impossibilium (nec-factus-nec-fieri-potuerit-aut-possit). T79 picks up **Notes V-VII**: Class IV (contra perfectiones physicae = edere/bibere/moveri/mori — contrary to divine aeternitas/immutabilitas/immaterialitas); Class V (mediate-creature-dependent — fides-in-Christum as *forma materialis* requiring intellectus+voluntas); Class VI (*simul et collective* vs *sigillatim et successive* — conservari + annihilari same creatura).]*

*[T77 — **Caput X § 7 Note II: Class I = contradictio-implicans***. ***Quam-impossibile-idem-simul-esse-et-non-esse, tam-impossibile-ea-quae-simpliciter-impossibilia-sunt-Deo-esse-possibilia*** — the Metaphysicians' + Theologians' constant view. Cross-refs: ***Martini Exerc. Metaph. II.4 theor. 20***; ***Scheibl Opera Metaph. II.3.16.3***. **Full Thomas Aquinas 1p q.25 a.3 citation**: *Deus-omnipotens quia-potest-omnia-possibilia-absolute* (not possibilia-naturae-creatae which-fewer; not possibilia-suae-potentiae which-circulatio); *possibile absolute = ex-habitudine-terminorum* (predicate not repugnans subjecto); *esse-divinum = infinitum, non-limitatum-ad-genus-entis, prehabens-totius-esse-perfectionem*; nihil-opponitur-rationi-entis-nisi-non-ens; hence contradictio *repugnat-rationi-possibilis-absoluti*. Thomas's elegant conclusion: ***convenientius dicitur, quod ea non possunt fieri, quam quod Deus non possit facere*** — Luke 1:37 *οὐκ ἀδυνατεῖ πᾶν ῥῆμα* interpreted: *verbum-contradictionem-implicans non-potest-esse-verbum*. **Johann Gerhard Exegesis Tomi I locus II de natura Dei et attributis divinis § 18** cites this + adjoins his ***ἐπίκρισις***: ***implicatio-contradictionis = repugnantia; quod-repugnat-fieri impossibile-est-fieri; Deum non facere ea quae contradictionem implicant***. **The anti-Photinianum/Calvinianum conclusion**: ***quanta protervia*** it is of the Photiniani-following-Calviniani-footsteps who say ***contradictionem implicare et simpliciter impossibile esse Deum esse in essentia unum, in personis trinum; Deum ab aeterno ex sua essentia generare Filium; divinam humanam naturam in Christo personaliter uniri*** — the Trinity + Incarnation targets. T78 picks up **Notes III-IV**: Class II (ex-hypothesi, facta-non-fieri-infecta — Agatho + Pindar + Sophocles + Eustratius + Jurists' virginity debate) + Class III (Deus Himself cannot *fieri*).]*

*[T76 — **Caput X § 6 + 4 Notes + § 7 opens**. **§ 6 Possibile Physicum vs Logicum**: *physicum* = *in-ordine-ad-potentiam-finitam* (Petrus-ante-generationem from parents' potentia-generandi); *logicum* = *in-ordine-ad-potentiam-infinitam = omnipotentiam Dei* (mons-aureus from Dei-potentia-creatrice). **4 Notes**: (I) signal use in Philosophia Morali + omni Theologia; those dismissing this distinction *saepius judicio labantur*; (II) possibile-physicum is relative to specific potency — *volare* possibile-avi non-homini (potentia-locomotiva ≠ potentia-volandi); *albedinem-videri* ad visus not auditus; (III) possibile-logicum triply-spectated — (1) just as non-repugnantia; (2) ability-to-be/fieri; (3) habitudo-ad-potentiam-Dei; three things said: non-sit + possit-esse-vel-fieri + possit-esse-a-Deo; (IV) possibile physicum/logicum often = possibile potentia-tali (though possibile has wider sense per § 2). **§ 7 opens**: *multa possibilia quae Deus non potest, creatura potest; et contra*. Scripture: ***Matt. 19:26 + Mark 10:27 πάντα δυνατὰ παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ***; ***Luke 1:37 οὐκ ἀδυνατεῖ παρὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ πᾶν ῥῆμα*** — yet many things God cannot do. **Note I's attack on Scholastic frivolous questions**: ***Utrum Deus loco Christi potuisset suppositare mulierem? Utrum Deus potuisset suppositare cucurbitam, et si suppositasset, quomodo illa fuisset concionatura, miracula editura, crucifigenda?*** — Veltheim detests their ***vanitas, petulantia, impietas***; invokes **Johann Gerhard** *(Theologi de Academia nostra universaque Christi Ecclesia longe meritissimi) Methodus Studii Theologici c. 4 p. 302 ff.* T77 picks up Note II: the list of *quae Deus non potest* — manifestissima-contradictio-involvens.]*

*[T75 — **Caput X § 5 Note II closes with Veltheim's defense + 4 Theological examples**. **V**: *Grotius satis expendit* — contradiction DOES appear in acts-adversus-ius-naturae (God cannot *lege-permittere-aut-praecipere-actum-necessario-disconvenientem*); (1) **Grotius's intent CLARIFIED**: NOT bis-duo-quatuor = jus-naturae identity, but both are *implicat-contradictionem* → both cannot be done by Deus; Deus *could* do both if either could come to be; (2) *agere praesupponit exsistere* conceded — but suffices to show manifest-contradiction prevents removal of obligation while homo remains; the ***actual-turpitudo vs possible-turpitudo*** distinction (ref back to Axiom I cap. 1). The Novatores' *fallacia-divisionis* in dividing Grotius's conjoined argument — like denying man/brute import contradictory-reasons just because not ens/non-ens contradiction. **VI**: sana-ratio formula + necessitas-hypothetica-vs-absoluta refuted above; **Scripture re-interpretation**: ***could God have proclaimed the contrary?*** Because God *salva-justitia-non-potuit*, hence ***datur omnino natura-immutabilis-justitiae communis-Deo-cum-hominibus***. ***Isa. V:3 worked*** (populus-Judaicum = vinea, Deus = cultori; vineyard-cultivator did all required). ***Mic. VI:2 worked***: Deus (summo jure Dominus) nevertheless asks men (vermes-terrae) to prove His actions' equity; the Hebrew-and-Greek textual exposition — *montes et colles = patriarchae (πατριάρχαι)*; *κρίσις τῷ Κυρίῳ* with Israel. **VII — the 4 Theological examples closing Note II**: (a) **John 8:43** Pharisees non-cognoscunt-sermonem (ex parte potentiae = auditus-impeditus-odio-veritatis; v.44 Patre-diabolo); (b) **1 Cor 3:1-2** Paul non-potuit-loqui-ut-spiritualibus (ex parte objecti = Corinthii-non-capaces-cibi-solidioris; lactis-potu-alui); (c) **1 John 3:9** natus-ex-Deo-non-potest-peccare (ex parte agentis = semen-Dei + Spiritus-S.-ductum-sequi + peccare contradictoria); (d) **Gal 4:15** oculos-eruere (ex parte objecti = cum-exitio-conjunctum). ***Talismodi exempla fere innumera in Sacris occurrunt***. T76 picks up **§ 6 possibile-physicum vs logicum** + 4 Notes + **§ 7 opens** possibile-respectu-Dei vs creaturae.]*

*[T74 — **Caput X § 5 Note II (continued): Grotius citation + Novatores' critique IV**. Veltheim's **provocatio ad communem Philosophorum/JCtorum/Theologorum consensum**: all presuppose existentia-iuris-naturalis + existentia-hominis; so long as *homo = animal rationale ac sociale* exists, *obligatio-ad-jus-Naturae tolli-nequit*. The contradictors' own definition of jus naturae: ***tali lege, quae ex generali conditione humanae naturae fluit, cujusque rationes ab universali humani generis conditione petendae sunt, quoque ex viribus ingenii hominibus congeniti et ex consideratione humanae naturae in universum investigari et cognosci et considerari possit***. **The massive Grotius DJBP I.1 § 10 n. 5 citation**: ***jus-naturale-adeo-immutabile-ut-ne-a-Deo-quidem-mutari-queat***; immensa est Dei potentia yet some things are *just-said-without-sense-expressing-the-matter*; Veltheim's commentary — repugnance *non ex-parte-Dei sed ex-parte-objecti*. ***Bis-duo-quatuor + intrinseca-ratione-malum-non-fit-malum*** parallel. **Aristotle citation**: ***ἔνια εὐθὺς νομισάμενα συνειλημμένα τῇ πονηρίᾳ*** (certain things judged bound with wickedness); the ousia/proprietates derivation. **Scripture catena** showing God *patitur-se-secundum-hanc-normam-judicari*: Gen 18:25, Isa 5:3, Ezek 18, Jer 2:9, Mic 6:2, Rom 2:6/3:6. **Novatores' critique IV**: (a) Grotius *non-satis-expendit* — bis-duo-quatuor contradiction differs from active-aversus-natura; (b) Grotius's own sana-ratio formula implies lex-Socialitatis injuncta a Creatore → circular; (c) homo-fortitus-naturam-socialem non-ex-immutabili-necessitate sed ex-beneplacito-divino → moralitas-actionum derivata ex eodem fonte, hypothetical not absolute; (d) Grotius's Scripture-interpretations re-interpreted: Heb 11:6 + Rom 2:6 Deus-remunerator/vindicator-ex-veracitate-sua + Abraham's appeal (Gen 18:25) + Isa 5:3 (just-omit-culture-oil-wasted) + Mic 6:2 (gratitude-necessarium-ante-omnem-legem). T75 picks up **Veltheim's point-by-point defense (V-VII)**: contradiction-argument proper response + comparison-ad-naturam-sana-ratione-utentem defended + Scripture re-interpretation; **four Theological examples closing Note II**: John 8:43 Pharisees-non-cognoscunt-sermonem (ex parte potentiae); 1 Cor 3:1-2 Paul-non-potuit-loqui-ut-spiritualibus (ex parte objecti); 1 John 3:9 natus-ex-Deo-non-potest-peccare (ex parte agentis); Gal 4:15 oculos-eruere (ex parte objecti).]*

*[T73 — **Caput X § 5 Note II opens: the MASSIVE IUS-NATURAE-IMMUTABILE polemic**. **Thesis statement**: Jus naturae is so immutable that not even God can change it — notable use in Moral Philosophy + Theology both Natural and Revealed. **Novatores' three objections**: (1) **derogates divine glory/immutability** — solus-Deus-aeternus-adeoque-solus-immutabilis, if law-can-be-changed-by-human-legislator why-not-by-Deus (manus-Domini-abbreviata); (2) **derogates divine omnipotence** — adeoque hoc modo circumscribere; (3) **derogates divine liberty** — Deus-condidit-hominem-ex-liberrimo-beneplacito-voluntatis + natura-hominis-sortitus-non-ex-necessitate-sed-ex-beneplacito-divino, so moralitas-actionum derivata ex eodem fonte (beneplacito). **Veltheim's refutation**: ***πρῶτον ψεῦδος = contradictors miss the true sense***. Thesis means: ***quamdiu homo exsistit*** et uti potest ratione+voluntate, obligatio-ad-actuum-necessario-convenientium-cum-natura-rationali-ac-sociali *tolli-nequit*; divine implicit-contradiction = willing ***aversatio-a-bono-sub-ratione-boni OR appetitio-sub-ratione-mali — absolute-simpliciter-impossibile***, repugnat voluntati-increatae AND voluntati-creatae. **The ignis-calidus analogy**: ***necessitas-existentiae vs necessitas-essentiae*** — just as true-fire conditioned-freely-by-Deo cannot-exist unless-existens-calidum, so jus-naturae cannot-dari-in-actu in-homine-libere-condito-a-Deo unless-sit-immutabile. **Perfect-vision analogy**: not-seeing-sapor/sonum does not derogate from vision (ex-parte-objecti); nor does not-changing-immutabilia derogate from God. **The silly novatores "si-non-homo-nullum-ius-naturae"**: *O miseram collectionem!* — as if anyone-ever-stated-ius-naturae-obligantem-hominem-antequam-existat-homo. T74 picks up: provocatio ad communem Philosophorum/JCtorum/Theologorum consensum + the massive ***Grotius DJBP I.1 § 10 n. 5*** citation (jus-naturae-immutabile ne-a-Deo-mutari-queat; bis-duo-non-sint-quatuor + intrinseca-ratione-malum-non-sit-malum parallel) with Aristotle contradiction-argument on οὐσία + Scripture (Gen 18:25, Isa 5:3, Ezek 18, Jer 2:9, Mic 6:2, Rom 2:6/3:6) + Novatores' detailed critique of Grotius IV.]*

*[T72 — **Caput X §§ 2-5 + Note I**. **§ 2**: causatum-possibile vs causatum-potentia — consequence from latter to former only; parallel to ens-possibile/potentia; causatum-potentia NOT verum-causatum. **§ 3**: *impossibile = non-ens-quod-nequit-esse-causatum-possibile* (two joint requisites). **§ 4**: investigator must discern ***ex quanam parte*** the impossibile says repugnance. **§ 5 triplex repugnantia**: (1) ***ex parte causati*** — *lapis non filius hominis* (generatio-passiva requires origo-viventis-a-vivente-in-substantia-sibi-simili); (2) ***ex parte causae*** — *lapis non pater hominis* (generatio-activa repugnat lapidi); (3) ***ex parte utriusque*** — *lapis nec pater nec filius lapidis*. **Note I**: diligence demanded; sense-genus examples — ex-parte-causae-repugnantia if ***completa-potentia-videndi non potest videre saporem/sonum*** (not visibilium); ex-parte-potentiae-repugnantia if ***caecus non potest videre coloratum/lucidum*** (visible-but-no-visual-potency); ex-parte-utriusque if ***caecus non videat saporem***. T73 picks up **Note II — the MASSIVE application to IUS-NATURAE-IMMUTABILE doctrine** (natural law so immutable even God cannot change it; Novatores' objections against Divine-liberty / omnipotence refuted via *necessitas-essentiae-vs-existentiae* and *homo-existit-liberrime-ex-beneplacito-Dei-sed-non-potest-non-habere-naturam-rationalem-ac-socialem*).]*

*[T71 — **Caput X Note II responses Ad IV-VI + Notes III-IV**. **Ad IV**: *vana collectio* — distinction (per Thomas Aquinas ***opusc. 27 de aeternitate mundi*** + ***Durandus of St. Pourçain 2 dist. 1 q. 2***) between creaturae-duratio ***quoad esse commune*** (abstractum from both — may equal essentia-Dei) vs ***quoad esse proprium*** (restrictus to creatura — absurd to equate). Creaturae-duratio *potest non durare* vs Dei-duratio *non potest non durare*. **Doctor Angelicus citation**: ***aliquid praeter Deum potuerit semper fuisse qua non ab eo factum = error abominabilis***; sed *aliquid semper fuisse et causatum a Deo* potest stare. **Ad V**: deny consequence. Formal + real distinction between aeternitas-Dei (absolute repugnat non-esse) vs aeternitas-creaturae (absolute non-repugnat non-esse). The Antitrinitarian maxim ***quicunque re ipsa et actu est ab aeterno, est verus Deus*** limited: only ***intrinsece et per essentiam*** — aeternitas-intrinsice-denominans-creaturae *absolute repugnat*. Immutability-of-creatura inference conceded with limitation (intrinsece-per-essentiam) — not against us. **Ad VI**: deny connection; (1) potentia-et-actus NOT formaliter dividant ens — corpus-naturale is Ens-but-neither-potentia-nec-actus; (2) habere-verum-esse-in-potentia-Dei = posse-creari-ante-creationem (no verum-ens-sequela); false-conclusion-syllogism exposing adduced-major. **Note III**: ***Paulus Voet, Gisberti filius, Juris in Acad. Ultrajectina Antecessor*** attributes negative view to Reformed in his ***Theologia Naturali Reformata c. 30 § 3 n. 7 p. 205 ff. ed. 1656*** with 13 contra-arguments; ***Thomas Campanella Metaph. 11.5.3 p. 25***. **Note IV**: ***Slevogt Vol. disputt. Academ. part. 1 disp. 9 § 18*** — ***in substantia intrinsice et per essentiam aeterna, ESSE et POSSE ESSE non differunt, sed FACERE et POSSE FACERE differunt*** — *non perinde Deo est suum esse ac suum facere*. *[T67 — **Caput IX § 9 Note IV: the massive Philosophico-Theological application on NOTITIA-DEI-CONNATA/INNATA**. **Core question**: *Num in nobis notitia quaedam natura insita de Deo detur?* All orthodox Theologians affirm. **Scriptural grounds**: (1) ***Rom. 1:18 ff.*** — Gentiles detain ***ἀλήθειαν*** in injustice; (2) ***Rom. 2:14-15*** — Gentes-faciunt-naturaliter + ***opus-legis-scriptum-in-cordibus***; (3) ***testimony of conscience*** with mutually-accusing thoughts; (4) **Patristic consensus**: Tertullian *de testimonio animae* + *Apol. adv. Gentes c. 17*; Arnobius *lib. I adv. Gentes*; Jerome *in Jer. XXVI.23* + *ad Gal. 1:15*; Damascene *fid. orth. I.1*. Gentilism anticipated: ***Epicurus apud Ciceronem lib. 1 De Natura Deorum*** + Cicero's own ***naturam ipsam impressisse omnium animis notionem Deorum***. **Theological terminology**: (a) ***lux + perfectio-habitualis-potentiae-cognoscenti-connata***; (b) ***habitus/dispositio*** — not habit proprie but ***κατ' ἀναλογίαν, imperfectum-habitum, quoddam-analogum-habitui, τελειότης quaedam potentiae intellectualis post-lapsum reliqua, cujus beneficio homo Deum quadantenus cognoscere possit***. Dissenting Philosophers hold intellective-potency = proximum-et-completum-principium (unnecessary to posit τελειότης). **The internal Theological controversy**: whether nullas-dari-Dei-notitias-in-actu-primo/secundo-connatas-aut-natura-insitas can be defended without heterodoxy. **Veltheim's Metaphysical mediation**: not his office to adjudicate; but Theologians must get *actus-primus/secundus/tale-in-actu-primo/secundo* FROM First Philosophy, else labor-perditus. **Precision**: those denying notitia-in-actu-secundo-connata reason that *actus-secundus always argues an act elicited by intellect ab-homine-ut-causa-efficiens* — hence not naturally-implanted. Those denying notitia-in-actu-primo-connata do NOT thereby deny the *lux-ingenita/habitui-analogum*, because *actus-primus-dicit-potentiam-causativam-eamque-completam* which requires ALL antecedenter-requisita — and ***species impressa*** (= *species intelligibilis*) is among antecedenter-requisita. So denying connata-notitia-in-actu-primo is compatible with affirming connata species-impressa + lux-ingenita; the inference *denies-connata-notitia → defends-nudam-potentiam-cognoscendi* is a manifestus error contra solida-primae-philosophiae-fundamenta. T68 picks up **Note V** (further Theological examples: Scripture perpetual efficacy; Mark 13:32 Christ's humana-natura-ignorance; pre-lapsarian sapientia; Bellarmine-vs-Lutheran peccatum-originis as concupiscentia in actu primo + motus-inordinati in actu secundo; fides-iustificans sometimes actus-primus sometimes actus-secundus) + **Note VI** Juridical-Political-Moral (dominium ex ***l. possessio 1 et dominiumque 1 D. de acquirenda vel amittenda possessione***; Grotius DJBP I.3.m.24 Rex-infans/furiosus/captivus Majestas as actus-primus-vs-secundus with Demetrius-Seleucus citation) + Caput IX CLOSES.]*

The potency can be complete when Sun actually illuminates (actu secundo) too. **§ 9**: ***causa-in-actu-primo vs secundo = non-vera-causa vs vera-causa***. Same for causatum-in-actu-primo vs causatum-in-actu-secundo. **3 Notes**: (I) parallel to ***ens-possibile vs ens-potentia*** cross-ref c.1 not.2 p.52: every ens-potentia ⊂ ens-possibile; every causa-in-actu-primo ⊂ causa-potentia (not conversely); ens-possibile can simultaneously be verum-ens (in sensu diviso); causa-potentia can simultaneously be causa-in-actu-primo; animal:homo+brutum :: ens-actu+ens-potentia; causa-potentia divided into completa (= causa-in-actu-primo) vs incompleta; causa-actu = causa-in-actu-secundo; (II) forward-ref to Caput X on *causatum possibile / potentia / in actu primo / in actu secundo*; (III) **absolute vs ex-hypothesi necessaria antecedenter-requisita** — fire-and-stipulae example: fire-can-be-combustion-cause-in-actu-primo without stipulae-applied (absolute non necessary), yet ex-hypothesi (if stipulae never applied, fire never cause in actu secundo); absolute necessary = one must be applied to other. *[T65 — **Caput IX § 7**. Key distinction: ***actus-primus ≠ id-quod-tale-dicitur-in-actu-primo***. Actus-primus = potentia-causativa / ratio-causandi (the completed-potency itself); *id-quod-tale-in-actu-primo* = *id-quod-habet-potentiam-causativam* = *causa-potentia / causatum-potentia* (the subject-bearer). Parallel for actus-secundus: actus-secundus = that by which cause is cause (= causalitas = illumination-process); id-quod-tale-in-actu-secundo = cause itself or causatum itself (= Sun qua illuminating / light qua produced). **The Sun-and-chamber example**: potentia-illuminandi-completa in Sun = *actus primus*; Sun with closed-valves windows at midday = *causa luminis in actu primo* but not actus-primus; Sun after valves removed = *causa luminis in actu secundo*; illuminatio-conclavis-facta-a-Sole = *actus secundus* / light produced = *causatum in actu secundo*. **3 Notes on the Causa-Naturalis difficulty**: (I) raises the puzzle — natural cause (= cause which necessarily acts when all antecedenter-requisita are present) seems unable to be in-actu-primo without immediately being in-actu-secundo; architect-case (= free cause) unproblematic; (II) **resolution via *active vs passive spectata potentia-causativa***: Sun's active-side can be complete (Sun ready to shine) while passive-side (conclave's receptivity) is blocked by closed valves — Sun is then *causa in actu primo* actively-considered. (III) Antecedenter-requisita *tripliciter sumi possunt*: active+passive simul; active-only; passive-only; the second-mode is operative when distinguishing *causa-in-actu-primo* vs *causa-in-actu-secundo*. T66 picks up **§ 8** (habens-actum-primum vs id-quod-tale-dicitur-in-actu-primo: consequence from latter-to-former only) + **§ 9** (causa-in-actu-primo vs secundo = non-vera-causa vs vera-causa) + Notes I-III (ens-possibile-vs-potentia parallel to causa-possibilis-vs-potentia; forward-ref to Caput X; absolute vs ex-hypothesi necessaria antecedenter-requisita with fire/stipulae example).]*

*[T64 — **Caput IX §§ 4-6**. **§ 4 antecedenter-requisita vs concomitanter-requisita**: ***antecedenter requisita*** = those which hold themselves ex-parte-potentiae-causativae (per Scholastic diction); ***concomitanter requisita*** = those which hold themselves ex-parte-causalitatis. ***Vision example***: antecedenter required on the side of sight = (1) objectum = color + lux; (2) medium = perspicuum (aer, aqua, crystallus, vitrum); (3) organon = oculus. Visus-incompleta if any of three lacking; visus-completa if all present. Notes: (I) ***voluntas-liberty-of-indifference preserved*** — ***posita-concomitanter-requisitis nulla potentia-causativa amplius indifferens est*** (concomitanter are of causalitas itself which determines potency to actually-cause); the saniori-judicio-praeditus-easily-advertit disclaimer against those who confuse the two to deny voluntas liberty; (II) the Scholastic ***extrinseca vs intrinseca causalitati*** distinction maps to antecedenter vs concomitanter. **§ 5 potentia-completa vs actus-primus latius/angustius**: every actus-primus is potentia-causativa, but not every potentia-causativa is actus-primus — only completa. Notes: (I) the Scholastic ***anima = actus primus corporis naturalis animati plantae vel animalis*** usage is not of this place; (II) the vulgar definition *actus-primus = forma-vel-natura-qua-esse-potest-principium-operationis* is too narrow — fails via passio-is-also-in-actu-secundo + formal/final causes also in actu secundo; ***actus-primus et secundus patent tam late quam causa et causatum***. **§ 6 actus-secundus**: *id, quo aliquid actu fit vel est vera causa* — reduce to Caput VIII § 13 pp. 548-549. Note: alternative definition *id-per-quod-potentia-causativa-immediate-sese-exerit* can be tolerated if rightly understood (fire-causing-heat-in-water via calefactio-as-actus-secundus); potentia-causativa never exerts itself unless actus-primus = completa. T65 next picks up **§§ 7-9**: habens-actum-primum vs id-quod-tale-dicitur-in-actu-primo distinction (ratio-causandi vs causa-potentia; Sun's complete illuminandi-potency vs Sun as causa-luminis-in-actu-primo); the same for actus-secundus; causa-potentia vs causa-in-actu-primo (ens-possibile vs ens-potentia analogy); causa-naturalis-neceßaria debate; **the massive Philosophico-Theological example on NATURAL KNOWLEDGE OF GOD** (notitia-connata/innata-de-Deo — Rom. 1:18 ff., Rom. 2:14-15, Patristic consensus Tertullian/Arnobius/Hieronymus/Damascene/Epicurus-apud-Ciceronem + the Theological controversy on notitia-in-actu-primo/secundo).]*

*[T62 — **Caput IX § 1 Notes VI-VII** — the massive Thomist-vs-Scotist controversy. **Note VI**: Scotus's formal definition of potentia-objectiva from ***2.dist.XII q.1*** — *non-repugnantia-secundum-quam-aliquid-aptum-est-ut-sit-objectum-potentiae-activae-divinae* (angel-not-yet-existing example). **Note VII**: full history of the Thomist-Scotist war. Root controversy = ***utrum materia prima sit Ens actu vel ens potentia*** — Scotists affirm per aliam existentiam, Thomists reject; Thomists' battering ram: ***si materia qua talis non habet formam, non habet actum***. Scotus distinguishes potentia-objectiva (= *actus entitativus* / *aequalis existentia* per Scotus / *transcendens-sive-praesentialis-existentia* per Johannes Magister / *objectivum* per Aegidius Romanus) from potentia-subjectiva (= actus formalis); Scotus denies ***omnem actum formalem materiae ut sic***, saves ***actum materiae ut sic entitativum***. **5 Thomist arguments** vs potentia-objectiva: (1) real-potency is active OR passive; (2) real-potency has real-respect to act; (3) if something is objected to active-potency, this means it is itself active; (4) non-repugnance = negation = nothing; (5) non-really-existens = ens-rationis = nothing. **Allied Nominalists**: ***Gabriel Biel 2 dist. XII q. 2*** (*Princeps Nominalium*); the ***Illustrious Count Jacobus Zabarella lib. 2 de rerum materia c. 2 p. 185*** (manifesto non dari). **Scotist counter-arguments**: (1) non-repugnance ⟷ repugnance by contradictory opposition — positive vs negative; (2) non-dependence on intellect-operation + non-negation = reale-et-positivum-quid; e.g. angel-can-be-produced parallel. **Scotist responses to Thomist 5 arguments**: (1) concede but mind the conclusion — formal-cause-informativa is realiter-existens but neither active nor passive; Rada controv. 12 art. 2 notab. 4 p. 379 cross-ref; (2) deny Minor — Scotus always holds real respect to actus-entitativus/aequalis-existentia; (3) deny consequence — shoemaker-art/leather analogy (*"ars sutoria is not the shoemaker"*); (4) deny Minor — repugnance negative vs non-repugnance positive-aptitude (immutability/immortality in God example); (5) deny Major — Thomist self-contradiction syllogism: *essences-of-things-did-not-exist-ab-aeterno-realiter → essences-ab-aeterno-were-entia-rationis* (against the Thomists themselves). T63 picks up **Note VIII** (three Scotist requisites of potentia-objectiva via Rada controv. de potentia creandi art. 1 p. 32 + massive final list of further Scotist defenders) + **§§ 2-3** (potentia-causativa in completam/incompletam distinction + completa formal definition).]*

*[T61 — **Caput IX § 1 Notes IV-V** — the heavy Scholastic-Theological apparatus. **Note IV**: Suarez's common definition — ***potentia causativa = ipsa potentia influens esse in aliud*** (*influere* taken laxius = *dare et communicare esse*); ALIUD = ens-non-ejusdem-numero-essentiae. ***Petrus/Paulus analogy***: Petrus and Paulus share human nature essentially-and-specifically but differ in singular essence (contracted + individuated via differentiae-individuantes); nature in them is multiplied/plurified. ***Trinity application***: potentia-qua-Pater-ab-aeterno-produxit-Filium + spiration cannot be causative, since three Persons cannot be aliud/aliud-atque-aliud. ***Thomas 1 part. qu. 25 art. 1 ad 1 p. m. 148*** + ***Cajetanus comment. in h.l.*** on *causa importat diversitatem substantiae* → ***name of causa ad intra never admitted in Trinity by Latin Doctors***; ***Vazquez 1 p. d. 131 c. 1*** on common Patristic sense that ALIUD neutraliter signifies diversity in nature; the ***Councils of Ephesus, Toledo, and Lateran c. Damnamus de summa Trinitate*** admit in Trinity ***alium et alium, non tamen aliud et aliud***; ***aliud suppositum in Trinitate*** admitted but not ***aliud simpliciter*** (= *alia natura* = *alia essentia*). Veltheim's digression on *communicabilitas multiplicativa*: divine essence communicable to several distinct persons but not ***cum sui multiplicatione*** (= one in three). ***Johannes Baptista Alonsorius Valentinus Bocairentanus Pandectae de universis*** eruditely treats; ***Suarez tom. 1 Disp. Metaph. Disp. XII sect. 2 pp. 171, 243, 244*** cross-ref; Aristotle did not define potentia-causativa in common. **Note V**: ***POTENTIA OBJECTIVA = vera-potentia-sed-non-causativa*** — creatures ***ante-productionem-ex-nihilo*** were in God ***not as actually existing but as effectus possibiles sive effectus possibilis esse in virtute suae causae***; expressly NOT in actu existentes (vs Sacred Scriptures) nor ***secundum similitudinem specificam*** (as from univocal cause) — God is NOT univocal cause of creatures (species-specialissima above God repugnat divine nature). God is ***equivocal cause***. **The massive eternal-creation-possibility defenders chain** — Patristic + Scholastic: ***Augustine XII de Civ. Dei c. 15*** + ***Ambrose Hexaem. XI.3*** + ***Athanasius or. 2 contra Arianos*** + ***Cyril Alex. VI.6 thes. c. 2*** + ***Damascene fid. orth. II.8*** + ***Hugo of St. Victor III de Sacr. c. 10*** + ***Albert the Great*** + ***Bonaventura*** + ***Marsilius*** + ***William of Paris*** + ***Henry of Ghent*** + ***Eugubinus*** + ***Nicholas of Cusa de venatione sapientiae c. 38*** + ***Raymond of Sabunde*** + ***Philoponus contra Proclum*** + ***Didacus Massus, Vallesius, Toletus, Bonaventura Baro Hibernus Clonmeliensis***. Contra: ***Aegidius Romanus, Scotus 2.dist.1 q.3, Pererius 15.13***. **Threefold-no-repugnance affirmative argument**: *ex parte Dei Creatoris / ex parte creaturarum / ex parte productionis*. ***From Scholastics the defenders***: ***Thomas Aquinas 1 pars q. 46 a. 2 + in 2.dist.1 q.1 a.2 + de potentia a. 14 + opusc. 27 de Aeternitate Mundi contra Murmurantes***, ***Durandus, Argentina, Capreolus, Dionysius Cist., Henricus Palatinus, Bassolis, Vazquez, Baconinus, Biel, Occam, Suncius, Javellus, Soto, Villalpandus, Aquarius, Ferrariensis, Isidorus de Isolanis adv. Averroystas, Arriaga, Suarez Disp. 26 sect. 6***. T62 picks up **Note VI-VIII** (Scotus's formal definition of *potentia-objectiva*; the Thomist-vs-Scotist controversy on *materia-prima-ens-actu-vel-potentia*; the three Scotist requisites for potentia-objectiva via Rada controv. de potentia creandi art. 1 p. 32) + § 2 opens *potentia-causativa in complete + incomplete*.]*

*[T60 — **Caput IX § 1 Notes II-III**. **Note II**: *esse potentiam* ⊃ *esse potentiam causativam* — the ***incomprehensibilis vis et foecunditas, qua DEUS Pater ab omni aeternitate ex sua substantia genuit Filium, qua Pater et Filius spirarunt Spiritum Sanctum*** is potency but not causative. Scholastic authority chain for the distinction: ***Scotus Quodlib. qu. 7***; ***Johannes de Rada Controv. Theol. part. 1 controv. 1 artic. 2 ad 1 p. m. 149***; ***Hurtado de Mendoza Disp. Phys. sect. 14 subf. 2 § 101 p. m. 350***; ***Franciscus Toletus 1. Phys. q. 2 quaest. 14 conclus. p. m. 252***; ***Petrus Fonseca Lusitanus lib. V Metaph. c. 1 quaest. 4 sect. 4 p. m. 526***. **The Rada long citation**: *potentia activa* bifariously received — (1) properly = *potentia causativa* (object = possibile opposed to ens-simpliciter-necessarium; everything other than God); (2) less properly = *potentia productiva* (object = every producible, including God). ***Pater aeternus habet potentiam productivam respectu Filii, non tamen causativam*** — the Father is not CAUSE of the Son, though He is His PRINCIPLE; causative-vs-productive distinction via *same-numerical-nature* criterion (cause ≠ effect in natura numerica; productive = can produce in same nature). **Note III**: ***potentia-generandi-active debate*** — Stahl + others deny on grounds that only *alius/aliud suppositum/alia persona* is produced; Rada admits via ***actiones ad intra / actus personales / actus notionales*** lens. The locked-in Theological doctrine: Son and Spirit produced NEITHER from any subject NOR from nothing (otherwise = creature) but ***from the substance of the producing principle*** — divine essence one+simplest+plainly indivisible, so Son and Spirit receive the ***same numerical essence whole and undivided***. Whatever its status (active or not), it is certainly ***not causative***. The distinction *potentia non-causativa vs causativa* commended by Theologian Scholastics AND nostrates Theologi as most useful and necessary. T61 picks up **Note IV** on Suarez's common definition of potentia-causativa (*ipsa potentia influens esse in aliud*) + Scholastic ALIUD-not-of-same-numerical-essence (Petrus/Paulus analogy + Trinity rejection of cause-ad-intra per Thomas/Cajetanus/Vazquez/Ephesine-Toledo-Lateran councils + Alonsorius Bocairentanus) + **Note V** on *potentia-objectiva* as vera-potentia-non-causativa, with the full eternal-creation-possibility defenders list (Augustine, Ambrose, Athanasius, Cyril, Damascene, Hugo-of-St-Victor, Albert, Bonaventura, etc. vs Thomas Aquinas + Durandus + Capreolus + Vazquez + Biel + Occam + Suncius + Javelli + Soto + Suarez).]*

*[T59 — **Caput IX opens: *De Potentia et Actu*** — § 1 *potentia causativa* definition + the enormous Note I on the multifariam-dicuntur significations of ***potentia***. **§ 1**: *potentia causativa* = *id, quo aliquid aptum est, ut fiat vel sit vera causa* (versus non-causativa). **Note I** = catalogue of 7 significations with heavy Scholastic apparatus: **(1) *non-repugnantia*** triplex per Stahl: ***Mathematica*** (via quantitatis-terminatio), ***Logica*** (via intellectus-operatio), ***Objectiva*** (via efficient-cause-actio); the Aristotle Metaph. V.XII citations with Greek ***καὶ μεταφορά ἐστι ὡς ἡ ἐν τοῖς γεωμετρικοῖς δύναμις*** + the three-mode-of-*possibile* passage. Veltheim's critique of the ***narrow-definition-of-potentia-logica*** reduces it to term-non-repugnance; expands to include exponible-proposition/conversa/syllogism-figure non-repugnances. **The massive *potentia-objectiva Scoti* doctrine**: Scotus's definition from ***2.dist.xii q.1*** in-ordine-ad-potentiam-divinam (eminenter vs per-conceptum-formalem); ***Johannes de Rada Aragonius Episcopus Padensis Controv. Theol. inter Thomam et Scotum part. II controv. 1 artic. 2 not. 2 p. m. 11*** cites Augustine (***de Civ. Dei XII.12*** + ***83 Quaest. qu. 46***) + ***Thomas Aquinas prim. q. 25 art. 4 ad primum p. m. 95***; the ***Suarez + Compton-Carleton*** confusion of Logica with Objectiva — Rodrigo de Arriaga + Scotus refutation; some confuse Objectiva with Passiva (confusion-note). **(2)** *potentia = vis/forma* rendering thing immutable (Aristotle loc. cit.). **(3)** potentia = *principium naturale* (Aristotle loc. cit.). **(4)** potentia = *habitus* — Aristotle ***Metaph. IX.2*** δυνάμεις ***ἄλογοι*** vs ***λόγου***; ***διὸ πᾶσαι αἱ τέχναι καὶ αἱ ποιητικαὶ ἐπιστῆμαι δυνάμεις εἰσί*** + ***αἱ μὲν μετὰ λόγου πᾶσαι τῶν ἐναντίων αἱ αὐταί***. Four translations compared: ***Bessarion Nicenus*** vs ***Johannes Argyropoulos Byzantius*** vs ***Ernestus Sonerus (Prof. Noricus p.m. 489)*** vs ***Alexander Aphrodisias (via Sepulveda Cordubensis)***. ***Dreier Phil. Prim. XIII § 4ff p. m. 228*** approves Alexandrine reading, firmly argues from ***Eustratius + Aristotle Metaph. 3.2, 2.3, 10.4*** that all sciences are *de contrariis*; rebukes those who try to evince liberty of intellect + will from this Aristotelian passage. **Seven distinct significations in Aristotle Metaph. V.9** mentioned as closure. T60 picks up **Note II** on potentia-causativa-vs-non-causativa with the explicit eternal-generation Trinity application (potentia-Pater-genuit-Filium is potentia but not causativa) + the Scholastic/Noster-Theologi cross-ref chain (Scotus quodlib. 7, Rada, Hurtado, Toletus, Fonseca) + Note III on the potentia-generandi-active debate (Stahl denies; others admit via *actiones ad intra*).]*

*[T58 — **Caput VIII §§ 14-17 — closes Caput VIII**. **§ 14 secondary requisites = *causa sine qua non***: necessary conditions on cause's side that cannot be judged cause/ratio-causandi/causalitas truth-saved; chamber-illumination through closed window-valves example. 6 Notes: (I) both requisites (necessity ex-parte-causae AND non-cause-non-ratio-non-causalitas) joint; (II) necessary vs necessary-ex-parte-causae — ***architectus-habet-cor*** example (heart is necessary but not causa-sine-qua-non of building); **(III) THE SCHOLASTIC ***causa-quae vs causa-qua*** DISTINCTION**: *causa quae* = that which has exerted ratio-causandi (sun as source of light); *causa qua* = the potentia-illuminandi exerting itself + illuminatio (causalitas = actio); (IV) vulgo definition understood sanely only if causa-quae and causa-qua understood simultaneously; **(V) MASSIVE PRACTICAL APPLICATION**: in Ethics ***natura-non-sed-actio-virtutis-causa***; in Politics the Jurisconsults ***cum Ulpiano*** say ***NUPTIAS NON CONCUBITUS SED CONSENSUS FACIT*** — *causa qua* = causalitas of marriage's efficient cause; *causa quae* of marriage = male and female; *causa quae* of virtue = man; nature-as-cause-of-virtue valid if you understand *causa qua*; (VI) ***SINE QUA NON = determinatio alienans*** — alters signification of ***causa***; Cicero *Acad. I*: ***Dialecticorum verba nulla sunt publica***; Metaphysicians have their notions/terms whose signification is from usu-in-scholis-recepto. **§ 15 causati-side**: three primary requisites paralleling causa — materiale-causati (shoe-potentia); ratio-causandi-passiva (leather's aptitude to be shoe); causalitas-passiva (effectio-calcei-ut-passio). Notes: (I) ratio-causandi activa ≠ potentia-activa-causativa; **causare lies wider than agere — pati etiam est causare** (matter receiving form causes composite); ratio-causandi active-spectata wider than ratio-causandi activa; (II) causalitas-active-spectata likewise wider than action; (III) two modes of attending to causati-requisites. **§ 16 causa materialiter vs formaliter spectata**: ***MUSICIAN-BUILDS-HOUSE*** (materialiter = per accidens; Music ≠ ars-οἰκοδομική); ***ARCHITECT-BUILDS-HOUSE*** (formaliter = per se; architectonica = perfecta ratio-causandi). **§ 17 causatum materialiter vs formaliter**: ***doctor-son-of-rustic*** (materialiter = per accidens; rustic is not true cause of doctor-qua-doctor); ***house-of-architect*** (formaliter = per se); ***son-of-father*** (formaliter per se — son-qua-son is from father, qui est vera causa). Final Notes: (I) full doctrine of *causa per se vs per accidens* reserved to peculiar chapter; (II) practical use of primary + secondary requisites reserved to peculiar chapter + more convenient method after some chapters. **CAPUT VIII CLOSES.** T59 opens **Caput IX — *De Potentia et Actu, inprimis illa potentia quam CAUSATIVAM, et actu, quem CAUSALITATEM appellant. Item de ACTU PRIMO ET ACTU SECUNDO, variisque eo spectantibus ac utilioribus distinctionibus.***]*

*[T57 — **Caput VIII §§ 7-13** — causatum formal definition + the three primary requisites of cause (materiale / ratio-causandi / causalitas). **§ 7**: ***causatum = Ens quod aliunde in esse suo procedit, ut tamen sit ALIUD respectu ejus, unde in esse suo procedit*** (shoe-respectu-corii-et-sutoris); Notes: (I) sufficient that causatum be *aliud aliunde procedens* — source can be ens (sutor) or non-ens (future-sale as *final cause*); (II) ***aliud suppositum ≠ aliud ens*** — Peter/Paul are both; three divine Persons are *aliud suppositum* yet one numerical ens (back-ref to § 5 Notes); (III) requisites now treated. **§ 8**: two kinds of genuine requisites — ***primaria vs secundaria***. **§ 9**: three primaria: (1) materiale; (2) ratio-causandi = *formale primum*; (3) causalitas = *formale secundum*. **Note = pedagogical imperative**: hardest questions in all disciplines concern cause-requisites, especially in practical disciplines; applicatio to the cause under consideration is key fruit. **§ 10 materiale**: id-quod-causa-esse-ac-dici-potest-salva-veritate (Peter is causa-aedificii but not qua-Peter — Peter-qua-Peter cannot be causa-aedificii, only materiale). **§ 11 materiale duplex**: ens-reale (Peter / causa-aedificii) or non-ens (inhabitatio as cause of aedificium-extructum, since inhabitation does not yet exist and may never exist — building may be destroyed by flame). Note: both ens and non-ens can be true cause — forward-ref to final/impulsive/objective causes doctrine. **§ 12 ratio causandi**: *id, quo aliquid aptum est, ut fiat vel sit causa* = *potentia causativa* = ***formale primum*** = ***actus primus*** = *causativitas* (barbaric Scholastic term); example — architect's art for house-cause; *potentia illuminandi* in sun for light-cause. **5 Notes** on the Scholastic *potentia-vs-actus* apparatus: (I) *nothing is cause unless able to be cause*; (II) actus-entitativus vs actus-qua-exsistere-potest paralleled by actus-qua-causa-potest vs actus-qua-causat; (III) causa-potentia vs causa-actu; (IV) causa-possibilis wider than causa-potentia; (V) **the full actus-primus/actus-secundus doctrine** — Scholastics distinguish between what has merely *potentia-ut-sit-causa-possibilis* (= *actus primus* via *ratio causandi*) and what has *actu-causa-esse* (= *actus secundus* via *causalitas*); causa-possibilis is prior, actu-causa posterior; *actus secundus semper praesupponit actum primum*. **§ 13 causalitas**: *id, quo aliquid est vera causa* = *formale causae* absolute = *causatio* = *causatio activa* = *actus secundus* = *actus causae absolute*; examples: *aedificatio* (house-causality); *illuminatio ut a sole procedit* (sun-light-causality). Notes: (I) causalitas:causa::existentia:ens; (II) *actus secundus/formale secundum* explained; (III) *causalitas = formale causae = actus*; (IV) *actus primus/ratio-causandi = potentia*; *causalitas = actus = causatio*; parallelism *per aedificationem aliquis est aedificans / per causationem aliquid est causans*. T58 picks up **§§ 14-17** — secondary requisites (*causa sine qua non*; cross-ref to Theological and Juridical ***causa qua*** usage — natura/actio for virtue; *consensus facit nuptias* with Ulpian); the ***causa materialiter vs formaliter spectata*** distinction (musician builds house = *materialiter* cause; architect builds house = *formaliter* cause); parallel ***causatum materialiter vs formaliter***; closes Caput VIII.]*

*[T56 — **Caput VIII §§ 4-5-6** with notes. **§ 4 adequate vs inadequate ALIUD**: adequate = neither includes nor is included (shoe/shoemaker); inadequate = includes or is included (shoe/leather). **Note = the *homo-est-mens* polemic**: *mens* defines man ineptly — *homo* and *mens* are inadequate-ALIUD-and-ALIUD, neither predicable of the other in casu-recto; the ***denominatio-a-potiori*** canon never meant essential-physical-definition should be made per *partem-essentialem-potiorem* — essentialis-definitio and definitum ***never realiter differunt***; essential definition is ***predicatio essentialis completa*** (whole essence in predicate). **Cross-ref forward to the planned Analytics work**: *disquisitioni locus est in Analyticis, quae fortassis Deo volente alias a nobis publicae eruditorum censurae subjicientur* — Veltheim promises publication, giving signal use: *officia et vitia docentium ac discentium*, reduced into disciplinary form. **§ 5 absolute vs cum-determinatione**: Theological Students must know — no Person is ALIUD absolute, but is ***ALIUD suppositum*** cum-determinatione; three Persons have ***one numero essentia*** but ***three numero subsistentiae/supposita***. Notes: (I) *aliud-aliud-ens* not in divinis, *aliud-aliud-suppositum* is. **(II) THE MASSIVE ANTITRINITARIAN POLEMIC**: their disjunctive — "either Son is ALIUD suppositum from Father (then not same essence) or is not (then not really distinct Person)." Orthodox response: no true contradiction, because not *simpliciter* affirmed of the same singular subject in the same mode — "non-ALIUD" treats ALIUD *absolute-et-simpliciter-in-sensu-affirmante* (= ALIUD *ens*); "ALIUD suppositum" treats ALIUD *cum-determinatione* (= ALIUD *persona/suppositum* with determined subsistentia); three really distinct subsistentiae / one numero essentia. Scholastic distinction ***ALIETAS essentiae vs ALIETAS subsistentiae*** — consequence does NOT hold from alietas-subsistentiae to alietas-essentiae. **§ 6**: ***Suppositum causae est causatum***. Notes: (I) every causatum is principiatum (back-ref p. 495 ff.); Scholastic coinages ***causare/causari*** paralleling activum/passivum; architect-causat-aedificium / aedificium-causatum-fuit-ab-architecto; (II) no classical verb equivalent; (III) ***causari-passivum ≠ causatum***: *id quod causatur* vs *quod causatum est* — with cause posited, *id quod causatur* is posited (not immediately *causatum*); with *causatum* posited, cause may no longer be posited (or no longer as efficient cause). T57 picks up **§§ 7-13** — causatum formal definition + two requisites + the three primary requisites of causa (materiale / ratio-causandi = *formale-primum = potentia-causativa = actus-primus*/ causalitas = *formale-secundum = actus-secundus = causatio*).]*

*[T55 — **Caput VIII § 3**. The great ALIUD-in-sensu-negante vs ALIUD-in-sensu-affirmante distinction with 6 Notes. **§ 3**: *sensu negante* = verum-reale-ens-non-ejusdem-numero-essentiae (shoe/shoemaker; act-of-using-medicine/not-yet-existing-health); *sensu affirmante* = verum-reale-ens-numero-diversam-essentiam-habens (shoe/shoemaker YES; act/health NO — health is non-ens, no essence; essentia-and-existentia realiter-non-differunt). In the Causae definition ALIUD must be taken ***in priori sensu*** (negante). **6 Notes**. (I) Two mere non-entia can be called ALIUD/ALIUD — blindness/ignorance — but only secondarily, extrinsically, with respect to the real entities (sight/knowledge); ***privationis essentia est absentia*** (Aristotle); pure-negation + privation differ in subject-capacity, so connote diverse-essence subjects; (II) ALIUD here taken *absolute et in primario significatu* — only verum-reale-ens; (III) *per modum substantivi* in Metaphysicians' usage; (IV) ALIUD-in-sensu-affirmante NOT excluded from Causae definition — abstracted, not repugnant; some causes are real entia, others are vera causa but not real ens (forward-pointer to final-cause doctrine); (V) from affirmante follows negante absolute-not-exclusive, not conversely — cross-ref to Caput VII § 8 (p. 505) on absolute vs exclusive principium cognoscendi. **(VI) THE MASSIVE TRINITY-vs-INCARNATION GREEK DISTINCTION**: Scholastics' precise usage — in Trinity ***alius, alius atque alius, ἄλλος, ἄλλος καὶ ἄλλος*** (three Persons; one essence); in Incarnation ***aliud et aliud, ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο*** (two natures; one Person τοῦ θεανθρώπου). ***Scholastici*** placed ALIUD in CAUSE-notion precisely to exclude ***actiones ad intra*** (eternal generation of Son + eternal spiration of Spirit) from being counted among causes — cross-ref ***Suarez Disp. Metaph.*** tom. I disp. 12 sect. 2 § 1 p. m. 243 ed. Mogunt. ***Augustine's*** "Pater Filio natura prior" repudiated by the Theological Schools as too broad; cause and effect can be ejusdem speciei essentia with father-and-son example in humans. T56 picks up **§§ 4-6**: ALIUD adequate vs inadequate (homo-est-mens polemic + Veltheim's planned Analytics cross-ref); ALIUD absolute vs cum-determinatione (Trinity tres supposita + ALIETAS essentiae vs ALIETAS subsistentiae); Antitrinitarian polemic (Son is non-ALIUD-ens from Father but cum-determinatione-ALIUD-suppositum from Father); causatum notion opens.]*

*[T54 — **Caput VIII opens: *De Causa et Causato*** (§§ 1-2 + 11 Notes = §§ 1 and 2's full apparatus). **§ 1**: *causa in communi = unde ALIUD in esse suo procedit, et essentiam suam habet aut accipit* (shoe accepts essence from shoemaker; shoe is from leather). Notes: (I) ***unde essentiam accipit et habet*** signifies cause-is-principle-and-indeed-principium-essendi — all preceding chapter must be sedulously recalled; (II) ***accipere-essentiam vs habere-essentiam*** distinction. **§ 2 the two requisites of true cause**: (1) must be *principium essendi* (*unde ALIQUID procedit*), (2) must be that whence ***ALIUD*** procedit — not every principle of being is cause (back-ref to Caput VII § 16 p. 523). (I) special study of *vox et notio ALIUD* — differentiates from mere *principium essendi*; (II) alternative definition *principium unde aliud essentiam habet aut accipit* — *principium* safely omittable since *unde* subintends it; (III) **the ANTI-SUAREZIAN polemic** — cause-notion is too common for exact definition; the variety of modes (ab aliquo / ex aliquo / per aliquid / propter aliquid / circa aliquid / impulsu alicujus / imitatione alicujus...) is not distinct by whole genus; Veltheim's refusal to be bound ***Ixionis rotae alligati*** to Suarez's demand (*Metaph. Disp.* vol. I Disp. 12 sect. 2 § 1) for abstraction from a proper, true, and real convenience; (IV) analytical breakdown — *principium* = quasi-generic concept; *unde aliud essentiam habet* = intermediate quasi-generic difference (equivalent to *principium essendi*, distinguishing from *principium cognoscendi exclusive sumtum*); *aliud* = ultimate quasi-specific difference. **(V) THE MASSIVE REVIUS-vs-SUAREZ POLEMIC**: the Conimbricenses + Suarez common definition ***causa est principium per se influens esse in aliud*** (from *Conimbr. II Phys. c. 7 q. 7 a. 1*), *canonized by the Pope of the Metaphysicians* (= Suarez, as Jacobus Revius calls him in his ***Suarez Repurgatus Disp. 12 Sect. 3*** p. m. 164): — "impropria" + "aversa a regula syntaxeos" (one does not *influo aquam in vas* but *infundo*; nor *fluvius influit aquam in mare* but *onerat*); ***febriculosa definitio: causa est, quae effundit esse in aliud. Est hoc rem definire, an involvere?*** Rodriguez de Arriaga's *Scholasticis gigas* elogium for Suarez in the preface of his *Cursus Philosophicus*; Revius's senile admission + continued reprehension; (VI) ***ALIUD*** is the decisive word distinguishing cause from any other principle — detailed treatment follows. T55 picks up **§ 3**: the great ALIUD-in-sensu-negante vs ALIUD-in-sensu-affirmante distinction with 6 Notes, incl. Scholastics' use of ALIUD to exclude actions-ad-intra (eternal generation + spiration of divine Persons) from causes, with the Trinity *alius/alius/alius* ἄλλος/ἄλλος/ἄλλος vs Incarnation *aliud et aliud* ἄλλο καὶ ἄλλο Greek distinction; cross-ref to Suarez *Disp. Metaph.* tom. I Disp. 12 Sect. 2 § 1 p. m. 243 ed. Mogunt.]*

*[T53 — **Caput VII, §§ 13-17 — closes the chapter**. **§ 13 wider vs stricter principium essendi**: wider = whence proceeds in-being either in-fieri or also in-facto-esse (shoe-from-leather both ways; shoe-from-shoemaker only in-fieri); stricter = only when in-facto-esse too (so leather yes, shoemaker no). Notes: (I) the ***unde-res-essentiam-habet-when-facta-est, inde-etiam-fiebat*** axiom; animal's organic-body + sentient-soul are *principia in fieri* and *in facto esse*; begotten animal no longer essentially depends on generans → generans only *principium essendi priori modo acceptum*; distinguish ***principium entis in fieri*** vs ***principium entis in facto esse*** (consequence valid from latter to former, not conversely); (II) this distinction is of *principium essendi* which is also *vera causa*. (III) **the massive anti-Reformed polemical note**: ***GRAVITER ERRANT, qui Patrem in divinis dicunt PRINCIPIUM ESSENDI respectu Filii*** — because their own definition requires continuing dependence after being-made, but from the ***Lutheran Symbolic Books*** it is manifest even to the simplest that ***no Person of the Divinity is either made or created***; eternally-begotten + eternally-proceeding — forward-pointer to Caput VIII (*De Causa*). **§ 14 ens-vs-non-ens principium essendi**: Physician (ens) and not-yet-existing health (non-ens) both principles of administered medicine; non-entities can be true causes (forward-pointer to doctrine of causes). **§ 15 internum vs externum**: leather (internal to shoe); matter+form (internal to composite); shoemaker (external); agent+end (external). Notes: (I) Metaphysicians apply this only to true-entity causes; (II) also to non-Entities (since non-ens cannot enter constitution); (III) ***the Physical privation-in-concreto doctrine*** — ***ex non-ente fit ens, ex non-homine homo, ex non-planta planta*** — treats privation-in-concreto as internal principle of generated entity. **§ 16 causal vs non-causal**: David as causal principle of Solomon; terminus-a-quo of journey, point of line, dawn of day as non-causal. **§ 17 close**: transfer all these distinctions mutatis mutandis to *principiata cognoscendi* and *essendi*. **CAPUT VII CLOSES.** T54 opens **Caput VIII — *De Causa et Causato, ac de utriusque necessariis requisitis, cum primariis, tum secundariis. Item de notione IDEM et ALIUD.*** Veltheim will build directly on this chapter: *cause = species of principle of being with the ALIUD-requirement*, and will treat first the Nicene *homoousion* and the ALIUD distinction between Persons of the Trinity (cross-reference back to the Note III anti-Reformed rebuke just shipped).]*

*[T52 — **Caput VII §§ 9-12** (further distinctions of *principium cognoscendi*). **§ 9 proper vs common**: proper to Physics = ***ex nihilo nihil fit***; proper to Morals = ***ex sua natura honestum est expetendum***; common to all = non-contradiction + excluded middle + *nihil est causa sui*. Notes: (I) every discipline uses both; (II) **the *proprium / quasi-proprium* distinction** — Metaphysical axioms are consideratione-proper-to-Metaphysics but usu-quasi-proper to any faculty via *praxi restringit* — Politician restricts to civil-order persons/things/business, Ethicist to moral duties, Theologian/Jurisconsult likewise; so most-accurate doctors sort doctrines into primary (from propria) and secondary (from quasi-propria, incl. Metaphysical axioms); (III) **the full Christological worked example**: *why does believer have hope of eternal life?* turns on ***posita causa ponitur effectus*** (Metaphysical) + ***quicquid Scriptura S. Canonica dicit, infallibiliter verum est*** (truly proper Theological); the heir-ius-successio Juridical parallel; (IV) ***philosophi utuntur rationibus, nos (Theologi/Jurisconsulti) utimur meris autoritatibus*** — true *cum grano salis* for the proper + ultimate principle; cross-ref to Caput Praeliminare § 41 ff. **§ 10 ultimate vs non-ultimate**: ***impossibile est idem simul esse et non esse*** vs ***quodlibet est vel non est***; non-ultimate = *proximum* = immediate/mediate; the *honestum-expetendum / promissum-servandum / ius-cuique-relinquendum* three-step chain. **§ 11 simpliciter vs in-genere**: simpliciter = non-contradiction; in-Theology-genere = *quicquid Scriptura S. Canonica dicit infallibiliter verum est*; in-Jurisprudence-genere = *quicquid ius civile sancit et approbat civiliter iustum est*. Notes: (I) cross-ref Caput Praeliminare § 47 ff.; (II) ***ultimum = primum*** — Metaphysics hands down the first fonts of any cognition. **§ 12 complex vs incomplex**: complex = integral proposition (Major/Minor); incomplex = middle term. Notes: (I) definition in middle-term place is complex-quid but not complex-principle (not integral proposition); (II) **the elegant Scripture-both-ways resolution**: ***quicquid Scriptura S. dicit infallibiliter verum est*** = *principium cognoscendi ultimum complexum* of Theology; but Scripture-the-term in that Major is simultaneously *principium cognoscendi incomplexum* of Theology; (III) same resolution for *ius civile* (one law vs complex of laws). T53 closes Caput VII with §§ 13-17 — the *principium essendi* distinctions, incl. ***the anti-Reformed Trinity-paternity-is-NOT-principium-essendi rebuke from Lutheran Symbolic Books***, then opens Caput VIII — *De Causa et Causato*.]*

*[T51 — **Caput VII §§ 7-8**. **§ 7**: principiatum parallels principium — fire-from-smoke, disease-from-urine are *principiata cognoscendi*; shoe-from-shoemaker/leather are *principiata essendi*. Civil law/testament/pact/contract in order to will are *principiata essendi*; moral acts cannot be imputed truth-saved unless the agent's will be their *principium essendi* — the Moral Doctors look into the *animus agentis*, the Jurisconsults with ***Ulpian*** say ***voluntas distinguit maleficia***. **§ 8 absolute vs exclusive**: *absolute* taken, every *principium essendi* can be called *principium cognoscendi* (matter/form of natural body); *exclusive* taken, only when NOT simultaneously *principium essendi* (smoke/fire; urine/disease). **9 Notes**. (I) *principiatum* parallel skipped as trivial mutatis-mutandis. (II) absolute case trivially evident — if a thing proceeds elsewhere in being, its cognition requires cognition of that principle. (III) **the *in sensu composito* clarification** — *principium essendi qua tale* ≠ *principium cognoscendi*; the thing itself ≠ the cognition of the thing. (IV) moral/political/theological/juridical teaching uses both. (V) **the Romans 1:19-20 locus classicus**: *illustre exemplum principii cognoscendi exclusive sumti nobis ipse Spiritus S. subministrat* — natural cognition of God from works of creation; the Gentiles are ***inexcusable*** because *aeterna Dei potentia* and ***θειότης*** can be known thence. Veltheim's crisp refutation of ***those who assert God has a principle because He has principium cognoscendi*** — the formally invalid consequence; "to have principium cognoscendi" = "to be able to be known from elsewhere." (VI) **Scripture as *principium cognoscendi exclusive sumtum* of the Trinity**: Trinity known-from-Scripture but not from-Scripture-in-its-being — Trinity ab aeterno, Scripture only in time, Trinity is author of Scripture. (VII) **the Juridico-Politico-Moral *signa* doctrine**: effects of right dependent on *animus* require sufficiently-indicated signs; signs lack mathematical certainty (men dissimulate in words and deeds); yet society cannot run on bare mental acts, so sufficiently-indicated acts are held true against the indicator — these signs are *principia cognoscendi exclusive sumta*. (VIII) ***an sit?*** questions in every discipline decided from principles of cognition exclusively taken — arguments from effect or sign suffice. (IX) **Christological grounding of combined cognoscendi+essendi**: *why does every believer have hope of eternal life?* — justification is cause (principium essendi) and principle of knowing simultaneously; *why is Christ super omnia diligendus?* — Christ's merit redeeming from power of sin/Devil/death. Cross-ref to earlier chapter 7 (pp. 377-381) for the full array of Theological/Juridical/Moral/Political examples. T52 picks up **§§ 9-12**: *principium cognoscendi* further distinctions — proper vs common (physics' *ex nihilo nihil fit*; morals' *ex sua natura honestum est expetendum*; universal axioms of non-contradiction + excluded middle + non-causa-sui); ultimate vs non-ultimate; simpliciter vs in-a-certain-genus (Theology's *quicquid Scriptura S. Canonica dicit infallibiliter verum est*; Jurisprudence's *quicquid ius civile sancit*); complex vs incomplex (Scripture both ways in the Theological syllogism).]*

*[T49–T50 — **Caput VII, §§ 3-close through § 6**. T50 completes **§ 3** by delivering the **second requisite of principle = priority** (shoemaker naturally prior to shoe = *Metaphysicorum dictio*); Notes: both requisites required jointly; Boethius definition — ***unde aliquid quocunque modo procedit***. **§ 4**: two requisites of principiatum = habitudo + posteriority. **§ 5 — where prius/posterius there ordo**: double cognitive order between cause and effect — in confused cognition effect-is-prior, in distinct cognition cause-is-prior. **Trinitarian application**: ***ordo naturalis enumerationis*** of the three Persons (Father 1st, Son 2nd, Spirit 3rd). Notes: (I) *nostro modo concipiendi* order has rei-veritas-foundation — the ***futuritio of Adam's lapse*** is prior to divine prescience of it (prescience is causal from futurition, not conversely); (II) **the David Pareus / Oxford-burned-by-decree-of-King polemic**: Pareus argued Rom. XIII makes the inferior Magistrate judge of the superior with capital-penalty right; Veltheim refutes with the *species intermedia* analogy from Dialectics — the inferior magistrate is not-private-to-inferiors but is-private-to-the-superior, so the Pareus argument contradicts itself; (III) order-axioms deferred. **§ 6 — the fundamental principium cognoscendi vs principium essendi distinction**: urine → disease, smoke → fire are *cognoscendi*; shoemaker → shoe, leather → shoe are *essendi*. The *voluntas*-as-principle application: for acts in the *genus morum* will is principle of knowing (Jurists cannot impute homicide-to-penalty unless *animus occidendi* is established — defense? punishment? offense?); and will is principle of being with respect to civil law, testament, pact, contract. Notes: (I) *principium cognoscendi* is principle of the *cognitio rei*, not of the *res qua cognoscitur*; (II) Analytics takes *principium essendi* otherwise than Metaphysics. T51 picks up **§ 7** (principiatum parallels principium — fire from smoke, shoe from shoemaker/leather) + **§ 8** with its massive 9-Note cluster on absolute-vs-exclusive principle of cognition, which carries (a) the Romans 1:19-20 natural-knowledge-of-God locus classicus for Veltheim's refutation of "God has a principle because God has principle of cognition," (b) the ***Scripture-as-principium-cognoscendi-exclusive-sumtum of the Trinity*** doctrine, and (c) the Juridical doctrine on *animi actus* requiring *signa*.]*
